tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

1	"""The agent loop (design §4): one chat turn as a stream of contract SSE events.
2	
3	    user message stored -> [LLM -> tools -> cards]* -> guarded text -> assistant message stored
4	
5	The LLM chooses tools and writes text; routes, prices and tickets come from the airline through
6	the four tools. Text is released sentence by sentence after the ReplyGuard traced every number
7	and city in it; the first problem replaces the whole reply with a code template. The turn's
8	quote cards become bookable only when `Airline.post_assistant_message` stores them (`done`).
9	
10	Nothing here can book: the loop talks to the airline through `Toolbox` (four tools, no booking)
11	and `post_assistant_message`. Booking is the HTTP endpoint's call, caused by the user's click.
12	"""
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import asyncio
16	import logging
17	import time
18	from contextlib import aclosing
19	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
20	from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable
21	
22	from ..airline import ConversationBusy, NotFound
23	from .context import build_context
24	from .guard import CityIndex, ReplyGuard, SentenceBuffer
25	from .config import EFFORTS
26	from .llm import LLM, Completion, LLMError, TextDelta
27	from .prompt import system_prompt
28	from .templates import fallback_reply
29	from .tools import DEFAULT_STATUS, STATUS_TEXT, TOOL_SCHEMAS, Outcome, Toolbox
30	
31	log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
32	
33	MAX_STEPS = 6
34	MAX_USER_CHARS = 2000
35	TITLE_CHARS = 60
36	LLM_UNAVAILABLE = "The assistant is temporarily unavailable. Your message was saved; please try again."
37	BUSY = "This conversation is still working on your previous message. Please try again in a moment."
38	INTERNAL = "Something went wrong. Your message was saved; please try again."
39	
40	
41	@dataclass(frozen=True)
42	class Event:
43	    """One SSE event of docs/api/contract.md: `name` and its JSON `data`."""
44	
45	    name: str
46	    data: dict
47	
48	
49	class _GuardFailed(Exception):
50	    def __init__(self, problems: list[dict]):
51	        super().__init__("reply guard")
52	        self.problems = problems
53	
54	
55	@dataclass
56	class _Turn:
57	    user_id: str
58	    conversation_id: str
59	    user_message: dict
60	    guard: ReplyGuard
61	    emit: Callable[[str, dict], None]
62	    reasoning_effort: str | None = None  # per-request thinking level; None = the client's default
63	    text: str = ""  # released so far
64	    cards: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
65	    outcomes: list[Outcome] = field(default_factory=list)
66	
67	
68	def message_view(message: dict) -> dict:
69	    """Contract `Message` of a stored row without quote cards (user messages)."""
70	    return {"id": message["id"], "role": message["role"], "text": message["text"],
71	            "cards": list(message["cards"]), "created_at": message["created_at"]}
72	
73	
74	class Agent:
75	    def __init__(self, airline: Any, llm: LLM, *, max_steps: int = MAX_STEPS,
76	                 ping_interval: float = 15.0, retries: int = 2, backoff: float = 0.5,
77	                 llm_timeout: float = 120.0, lock_timeout: float | None = 120.0,
78	                 sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep):
79	        self.llm = llm
80	        self.store = airline.store
81	        self.max_steps = max_steps
82	        self.ping_interval = ping_interval
83	        self.retries = retries
84	        self.backoff = backoff
85	        self.llm_timeout = llm_timeout
86	        self.lock_timeout = lock_timeout
87	        self._sleep = sleep
88	        self._tools = Toolbox(airline)
89	        # The only other things the loop takes from the airline. No reference to the Airline
90	        # object itself is kept.
91	        self._post_assistant_message = airline.post_assistant_message
92	        self._locks = airline.locks
93	        self._networks = airline.networks
94	        self._index: tuple[str, CityIndex] | None = None
95	        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
96	
97	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ public -------------
98	    def stream_turn(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, *,
99	                    reasoning_effort: str | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[Event]:
100	        """Start a turn and return its events: `user_message`, then `status` / `card` / `delta` /
101	        `replace` / `ping`, ending with exactly one `done` or `error`.
102	
103	        `reasoning_effort` overrides the LLM's thinking level for this turn (none / low / high /
104	        max; None = configured default).
105	
106	        Raises before anything is stored: NotFound (not the user's conversation), ValueError
107	        (empty or too long text, unknown reasoning_effort). Must be called on the event loop. The turn runs in its own
108	        task: it finishes and is stored even when the client stops reading."""
109	        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
110	            raise ValueError("text must not be empty")
111	        text = text.strip()
112	        if len(text) > MAX_USER_CHARS:
113	            raise ValueError(f"text is longer than {MAX_USER_CHARS} characters")
114	        if reasoning_effort is not None and reasoning_effort not in EFFORTS:
115	            raise ValueError(f"reasoning_effort must be one of {', '.join(EFFORTS)}")
116	        if self.store.get_conversation(user_id, conversation_id) is None:
117	            raise NotFound(conversation_id)
118	        queue: asyncio.Queue[Event | None] = asyncio.Queue()
119	        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
120	            self._run(user_id, conversation_id, text, reasoning_effort, queue))
121	        self._tasks.add(task)
122	        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)
123	        return self._events(queue)
124	
125	    async def wait_idle(self) -> None:
126	        """Wait for every running turn (shutdown, tests)."""
127	        while pending := [t for t in self._tasks if not t.done()]:
128	            await asyncio.wait(pending)
129	
130	    async def _events(self, queue: asyncio.Queue) -> AsyncIterator[Event]:
131	        while True:
132	            try:
133	                event = await asyncio.wait_for(queue.get(), self.ping_interval)
134	            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
135	                yield Event("ping", {})
136	                continue
137	            if event is None:
138	                return
139	            yield event
140	
141	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ one turn -----------
142	    async def _run(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, reasoning_effort: str | None,
143	                   queue: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
144	        def emit(name: str, data: dict) -> None:
145	            queue.put_nowait(Event(name, data))
146	
147	        try:
148	            async with self._locks.hold_async(conversation_id, timeout=self.lock_timeout):
149	                await self._turn(user_id, conversation_id, text, reasoning_effort, emit)
150	        except ConversationBusy:
151	            emit("error", {"code": "conversation_busy", "message": BUSY})
152	        except Exception:
153	            log.exception("chat turn failed (conversation %s)", conversation_id)
154	            emit("error", {"code": "internal_error", "message": INTERNAL})
155	        finally:
156	            queue.put_nowait(None)
157	
158	    async def _turn(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, reasoning_effort: str | None,
159	                    emit: Callable[[str, dict], None]) -> None:
160	        store = self.store
161	        conversation = await asyncio.to_thread(store.get_conversation, user_id, conversation_id)
162	        user_message = await asyncio.to_thread(store.add_message, user_id, conversation_id, "user", text)
163	        emit("user_message", message_view(user_message))
164	        if conversation is not None and not conversation["title"]:
165	            await asyncio.to_thread(store.set_conversation_title, user_id, conversation_id,
166	                                    " ".join(text.split())[:TITLE_CHARS])
167	
168	        context = await asyncio.to_thread(build_context, store, user_id, conversation_id)
169	        index = await asyncio.to_thread(self._city_index)
170	        today = store.clock().date()
171	        guard = ReplyGuard(index, records=context.records, user_text=text,
172	                           earlier_user_texts=context.user_texts[:-1], today=today)
173	        turn = _Turn(user_id, conversation_id, user_message, guard, emit, reasoning_effort)
174	        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt(today)}, *context.messages]
175	
176	        for _ in range(self.max_steps):
177	            try:
178	                completion = await self._llm_step(turn, messages)
179	            except _GuardFailed as failed:
180	                return await self._finish(turn, fallback=failed.problems)
181	            except LLMError as exc:
182	                if not turn.outcomes and not turn.text:
183	                    emit("error", {"code": "llm_unavailable", "message": LLM_UNAVAILABLE})
184	                    return
185	                return await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "llm_error", "value": str(exc)[:200]}])
186	            if not completion.tool_calls:
187	                if not turn.text.strip():
188	                    return await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "empty_reply", "value": ""}])
189	                return await self._finish(turn)
190	            messages.append(completion.assistant_message())
191	            for call in completion.tool_calls:
192	                emit("status", {"text": STATUS_TEXT.get(call["name"], DEFAULT_STATUS)})
193	                outcome = await asyncio.to_thread(self._tools.run, user_id, conversation_id,
194	                                                  call["name"], call["arguments"])
195	                await asyncio.to_thread(
196	                    store.add_tool_call, user_id, user_message["id"], outcome.name, outcome.args,
197	                    outcome.payload, error=outcome.error, latency_ms=outcome.latency_ms)
198	                turn.outcomes.append(outcome)
199	                guard.add_record(outcome.payload)
200	                for card in outcome.cards:
201	                    turn.cards.append(card)
202	                    emit("card", {"card": card})
203	                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": outcome.for_llm()})
204	        await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "max_steps", "value": str(self.max_steps)}])
205	
206	    async def _finish(self, turn: _Turn, fallback: list[dict] | None = None) -> None:
207	        """Persist the assistant message (the `done` moment: quote cards become bookable)."""
208	        text = turn.text.rstrip()
209	        if fallback is not None:
210	            text = fallback_reply(turn.outcomes)
211	            turn.emit("replace", {"text": text})
212	        message = await asyncio.to_thread(
213	            self._post_assistant_message, turn.user_id, turn.conversation_id, text, turn.cards, fallback)
214	        turn.emit("done", {"message": message})
215	
216	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ LLM step -----------
217	    def _release(self, turn: _Turn, piece: str) -> None:
218	        """Check the reply so far plus `piece`; send `piece` when nothing is wrong. Checking the
219	        whole text catches a number or a city name that spans two pieces (`St. | Louis`)."""
220	        if not turn.text:
221	            piece = piece.lstrip()
222	        elif not turn.text[-1].isspace() and not piece[:1].isspace():
223	            piece = "\n\n" + piece  # text of a later step starts a new paragraph
224	        problems = turn.guard.check(turn.text + piece)
225	        if problems:
226	            raise _GuardFailed(problems)
227	        turn.text += piece
228	        turn.emit("delta", {"text": piece})
229	
230	    async def _llm_step(self, turn: _Turn, messages: list[dict]) -> Completion:
231	        """One LLM call with retries. Text is released as it streams. A failed call is retried
232	        only while none of its text has been released."""
233	        request = {"turn": turn.user_message["id"], "messages": list(messages),
234	                   "tools": [t["function"]["name"] for t in TOOL_SCHEMAS],
235	                   "reasoning_effort": turn.reasoning_effort or getattr(self.llm, "reasoning_effort", None)}
236	        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):
237	            started = time.monotonic()
238	            buffer = SentenceBuffer()
239	            completion: Completion | None = None
240	            released = False
241	            content = blank = ""
242	
243	            def log_call(response: dict, tokens: int | None = None) -> Awaitable[Any]:
244	                return asyncio.to_thread(
245	                    self.store.add_llm_call, turn.user_id, turn.conversation_id, request, response,
246	                    latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000), tokens=tokens,
247	                    model=getattr(self.llm, "model", None))
248	
249	            try:
250	                # aclosing: a guard failure or a timeout must close the HTTP stream right away
251	                async with asyncio.timeout(self.llm_timeout), \
252	                        aclosing(self.llm.stream(
253	                            messages, TOOL_SCHEMAS, reasoning_effort=turn.reasoning_effort)) as stream:
254	                    async for event in stream:
255	                        if isinstance(event, TextDelta):
256	                            content += event.text
257	                            for sentence in buffer.push(event.text):
258	                                if sentence.strip():
259	                                    self._release(turn, blank + sentence)
260	                                    blank, released = "", True
261	                                else:
262	                                    blank += sentence  # white space is never sent on its own
263	                        else:
264	                            completion = event
265	                if completion is None:
266	                    raise LLMError("LLM stream ended without a completion", retryable=True)
267	                rest = buffer.flush()
268	                if rest.strip():
269	                    self._release(turn, blank + rest)
270	            except _GuardFailed as failed:
271	                await log_call({"content": content, "guard_problems": failed.problems, "aborted": True})
272	                raise
273	            except (LLMError, TimeoutError) as exc:
274	                error = exc if isinstance(exc, LLMError) else LLMError("LLM call timed out", retryable=True)
275	                await log_call({"content": content, "error": str(error)[:300], "attempt": attempt + 1})
276	                if released or not error.retryable or attempt == self.retries:
277	                    raise error from None
278	                await self._sleep(self.backoff * 2 ** attempt)
279	                continue
280	            await log_call(completion.as_record(), completion.total_tokens)
281	            return completion
282	        raise LLMError("unreachable", retryable=False)  # pragma: no cover
283	
284	    def _city_index(self) -> CityIndex:
285	        """City names for the guard, from the airline's current network (rebuilt when
286	        locations.db changes)."""
287	        net = self._networks.current()
288	        if self._index is None or self._index[0] != net.fingerprint.id:
289	            self._index = (net.fingerprint.id, CityIndex(net.cities))
290	        return self._index[1]
291

quote cards become bookable only when `Airline.post_assistant_message` stores them (`done`).

Nothing here can book: the loop talks to the airline through `Toolbox` (four tools, no booking)
and `post_assistant_message`. Booking is the HTTP endpoint's call, caused by the user's click.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import logging
import time
from contextlib import aclosing
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

from ..airline import ConversationBusy, NotFound
from .context import build_context
from .guard import CityIndex, ReplyGuard, SentenceBuffer
from .config import EFFORTS
from .llm import LLM, Completion, LLMError, TextDelta
from .prompt import system_prompt
from .templates import fallback_reply

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_STEPS = 6
MAX_USER_CHARS = 2000
TITLE_CHARS = 60
LLM_UNAVAILABLE = "The assistant is temporarily unavailable. Your message was saved; please try again."
BUSY = "This conversation is still working on your previous message. Please try again in a moment."
INTERNAL = "Something went wrong. Your message was saved; please try again."


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """One SSE event of docs/api/contract.md: `name` and its JSON `data`."""

    name: str
    data: dict


class _GuardFailed(Exception):
    def __init__(self, problems: list[dict]):
        super().__init__("reply guard")
        self.problems = problems


@dataclass
class _Turn:
    user_id: str
    conversation_id: str
    user_message: dict
    guard: ReplyGuard
    emit: Callable[[str, dict], None]
    reasoning_effort: str | None = None  # per-request thinking level; None = the client's default
    text: str = ""  # released so far
    cards: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)
    outcomes: list[Outcome] = field(default_factory=list)


def message_view(message: dict) -> dict:
    """Contract `Message` of a stored row without quote cards (user messages)."""
    return {"id": message["id"], "role": message["role"], "text": message["text"],
            "cards": list(message["cards"]), "created_at": message["created_at"]}


class Agent:
    def __init__(self, airline: Any, llm: LLM, *, max_steps: int = MAX_STEPS,
                 ping_interval: float = 15.0, retries: int = 2, backoff: float = 0.5,
                 llm_timeout: float = 120.0, lock_timeout: float | None = 120.0,
                 sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep):
        self.llm = llm
        self.store = airline.store
        self.max_steps = max_steps
        self.ping_interval = ping_interval
        self.retries = retries
        self.backoff = backoff
        self.llm_timeout = llm_timeout
        self.lock_timeout = lock_timeout
        self._sleep = sleep
        self._tools = Toolbox(airline)
        # The only other things the loop takes from the airline. No reference to the Airline
        # object itself is kept.
        self._post_assistant_message = airline.post_assistant_message
        self._locks = airline.locks
        self._networks = airline.networks
        self._index: tuple[str, CityIndex] | None = None
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ public -------------
    def stream_turn(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, *,
                    reasoning_effort: str | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[Event]:
        """Start a turn and return its events: `user_message`, then `status` / `card` / `delta` /
        `replace` / `ping`, ending with exactly one `done` or `error`.

        `reasoning_effort` overrides the LLM's thinking level for this turn (none / low / high /
        max; None = configured default).

        Raises before anything is stored: NotFound (not the user's conversation), ValueError
        (empty or too long text, unknown reasoning_effort). Must be called on the event loop. The turn runs in its own
        task: it finishes and is stored even when the client stops reading."""
        if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
            raise ValueError("text must not be empty")
        text = text.strip()
        if len(text) > MAX_USER_CHARS:
            raise ValueError(f"text is longer than {MAX_USER_CHARS} characters")
        if reasoning_effort is not None and reasoning_effort not in EFFORTS:
            raise ValueError(f"reasoning_effort must be one of {', '.join(EFFORTS)}")
        if self.store.get_conversation(user_id, conversation_id) is None:
            raise NotFound(conversation_id)
        queue: asyncio.Queue[Event | None] = asyncio.Queue()
        task = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(
            self._run(user_id, conversation_id, text, reasoning_effort, queue))
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)
        return self._events(queue)

    async def wait_idle(self) -> None:
        """Wait for every running turn (shutdown, tests)."""
        while pending := [t for t in self._tasks if not t.done()]:
            await asyncio.wait(pending)

    async def _events(self, queue: asyncio.Queue) -> AsyncIterator[Event]:
        while True:
            try:
                event = await asyncio.wait_for(queue.get(), self.ping_interval)
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                yield Event("ping", {})
                continue
            if event is None:
                return
            yield event

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ one turn -----------
    async def _run(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, reasoning_effort: str | None,
                   queue: asyncio.Queue) -> None:
        def emit(name: str, data: dict) -> None:
            queue.put_nowait(Event(name, data))

        try:
            async with self._locks.hold_async(conversation_id, timeout=self.lock_timeout):
                await self._turn(user_id, conversation_id, text, reasoning_effort, emit)
        except ConversationBusy:
            emit("error", {"code": "conversation_busy", "message": BUSY})
        except Exception:
            log.exception("chat turn failed (conversation %s)", conversation_id)
            emit("error", {"code": "internal_error", "message": INTERNAL})
        finally:
            queue.put_nowait(None)

    async def _turn(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, text: str, reasoning_effort: str | None,
                    emit: Callable[[str, dict], None]) -> None:
        store = self.store
        conversation = await asyncio.to_thread(store.get_conversation, user_id, conversation_id)
        user_message = await asyncio.to_thread(store.add_message, user_id, conversation_id, "user", text)
        emit("user_message", message_view(user_message))
        if conversation is not None and not conversation["title"]:
            await asyncio.to_thread(store.set_conversation_title, user_id, conversation_id,
                                    " ".join(text.split())[:TITLE_CHARS])

        context = await asyncio.to_thread(build_context, store, user_id, conversation_id)
        index = await asyncio.to_thread(self._city_index)
        today = store.clock().date()
        guard = ReplyGuard(index, records=context.records, user_text=text,
                           earlier_user_texts=context.user_texts[:-1], today=today)
        turn = _Turn(user_id, conversation_id, user_message, guard, emit, reasoning_effort)
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt(today)}, *context.messages]

        for _ in range(self.max_steps):
            try:
                completion = await self._llm_step(turn, messages)
            except _GuardFailed as failed:
                return await self._finish(turn, fallback=failed.problems)
            except LLMError as exc:
                if not turn.outcomes and not turn.text:
                    emit("error", {"code": "llm_unavailable", "message": LLM_UNAVAILABLE})
                    return
                return await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "llm_error", "value": str(exc)[:200]}])
            if not completion.tool_calls:
                if not turn.text.strip():
                    return await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "empty_reply", "value": ""}])
                return await self._finish(turn)
            messages.append(completion.assistant_message())
            for call in completion.tool_calls:
                emit("status", {"text": STATUS_TEXT.get(call["name"], DEFAULT_STATUS)})
                outcome = await asyncio.to_thread(self._tools.run, user_id, conversation_id,
                                                  call["name"], call["arguments"])
                await asyncio.to_thread(
                    store.add_tool_call, user_id, user_message["id"], outcome.name, outcome.args,
                    outcome.payload, error=outcome.error, latency_ms=outcome.latency_ms)
                turn.outcomes.append(outcome)
                guard.add_record(outcome.payload)
                for card in outcome.cards:
                    turn.cards.append(card)
                    emit("card", {"card": card})
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": outcome.for_llm()})
        await self._finish(turn, fallback=[{"kind": "max_steps", "value": str(self.max_steps)}])

    async def _finish(self, turn: _Turn, fallback: list[dict] | None = None) -> None:
        """Persist the assistant message (the `done` moment: quote cards become bookable)."""
        text = turn.text.rstrip()
        if fallback is not None:
            text = fallback_reply(turn.outcomes)
            turn.emit("replace", {"text": text})
        message = await asyncio.to_thread(
            self._post_assistant_message, turn.user_id, turn.conversation_id, text, turn.cards, fallback)
        turn.emit("done", {"message": message})

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ LLM step -----------
    def _release(self, turn: _Turn, piece: str) -> None:
        """Check the reply so far plus `piece`; send `piece` when nothing is wrong. Checking the
        whole text catches a number or a city name that spans two pieces (`St. | Louis`)."""
        if not turn.text:
            piece = piece.lstrip()
        elif not turn.text[-1].isspace() and not piece[:1].isspace():
            piece = "\n\n" + piece  # text of a later step starts a new paragraph
        problems = turn.guard.check(turn.text + piece)
        if problems:
            raise _GuardFailed(problems)
        turn.text += piece
        turn.emit("delta", {"text": piece})

    async def _llm_step(self, turn: _Turn, messages: list[dict]) -> Completion:
        """One LLM call with retries. Text is released as it streams. A failed call is retried
        only while none of its text has been released."""
        request = {"turn": turn.user_message["id"], "messages": list(messages),
                   "tools": [t["function"]["name"] for t in TOOL_SCHEMAS],
                   "reasoning_effort": turn.reasoning_effort or getattr(self.llm, "reasoning_effort", None)}
        for attempt in range(self.retries + 1):
            started = time.monotonic()
            buffer = SentenceBuffer()
            completion: Completion | None = None
            released = False
            content = blank = ""

            def log_call(response: dict, tokens: int | None = None) -> Awaitable[Any]:
                return asyncio.to_thread(
                    self.store.add_llm_call, turn.user_id, turn.conversation_id, request, response,
                    latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000), tokens=tokens,
                    model=getattr(self.llm, "model", None))

            try:
                # aclosing: a guard failure or a timeout must close the HTTP stream right away
                async with asyncio.timeout(self.llm_timeout), \
                        aclosing(self.llm.stream(
                            messages, TOOL_SCHEMAS, reasoning_effort=turn.reasoning_effort)) as stream:
                    async for event in stream:
                        if isinstance(event, TextDelta):
                            content += event.text
                            for sentence in buffer.push(event.text):
                                if sentence.strip():
                                    self._release(turn, blank + sentence)
                                    blank, released = "", True
                                else:
                                    blank += sentence  # white space is never sent on its own
                        else:
                            completion = event
                if completion is None:
                    raise LLMError("LLM stream ended without a completion", retryable=True)
                rest = buffer.flush()
                if rest.strip():
                    self._release(turn, blank + rest)
            except _GuardFailed as failed:
                await log_call({"content": content, "guard_problems": failed.problems, "aborted": True})
                raise
            except (LLMError, TimeoutError) as exc:
                error = exc if isinstance(exc, LLMError) else LLMError("LLM call timed out", retryable=True)
                await log_call({"content": content, "error": str(error)[:300], "attempt": attempt + 1})
                if released or not error.retryable or attempt == self.retries:
                    raise error from None
                await self._sleep(self.backoff * 2 ** attempt)
                continue
            await log_call(completion.as_record(), completion.total_tokens)
            return completion
        raise LLMError("unreachable", retryable=False)  # pragma: no cover

    def _city_index(self) -> CityIndex:
        """City names for the guard, from the airline's current network (rebuilt when
        locations.db changes)."""
        net = self._networks.current()
        if self._index is None or self._index[0] != net.fingerprint.id:
            self._index = (net.fingerprint.id, CityIndex(net.cities))
        return self._index[1]

232	        scan = _scan(text)
233	        for written, value in scan.numbers:
234	            if value not in self.numbers:
235	                problems.append({"kind": "number", "value": written})
236	        for written, (year, month, day) in scan.dates:
237	            known = ((year, month, day) in self.dates if year is not None
238	                     else (month, day) in self._partial_dates
239	                     or any((m, d) == (month, day) for _, m, d in self.dates))
240	            if not known:
241	                problems.append({"kind": "date", "value": written})
242	        for written, hhmm in scan.times:
243	            if hhmm not in self.times:
244	                problems.append({"kind": "time", "value": written})
245	        for written in scan.ids:
246	            if written not in self.ids:
247	                problems.append({"kind": "id", "value": written})
248	        for mention in self.index.mentions(text):
249	            if not self.cities.intersection(mention.cities):
250	                problems.append({"kind": "city", "value": mention.text})
251	        return problems
252	
253	
254	# --- sentence buffering for the stream ------------------------------------------------------
255	_SENTENCE = re.compile(r".*?(?:[.!?]+(?=\s)\s+|[。！？]+|\n+)", re.S)
256	
257	
258	class SentenceBuffer:
259	    """Cuts streamed text into sentences. A cut is made only after sentence punctuation followed
260	    by white space, after CJK sentence punctuation, or after a line break - never inside a number
261	    such as `1,160.71`. Each piece keeps its trailing white space, so the pieces concatenate to
262	    the original text."""
263	
264	    def __init__(self) -> None:
265	        self._buf = ""
266	
267	    def push(self, chunk: str) -> list[str]:
268	        self._buf += chunk
269	        out = []
270	        pos = 0
271	        while True:
272	            m = _SENTENCE.match(self._buf, pos)
273	            if m is None:
274	                break
275	            # white space at the very end may still grow; that is harmless, the next piece
276	            # simply starts with it
277	            out.append(m.group(0))
278	            pos = m.end()
279	        self._buf = self._buf[pos:]
280	        return out
281	
282	    def flush(self) -> str:
283	        rest, self._buf = self._buf, ""
284	        return rest
285

1	"""The four tools the LLM can call: schemas, argument validation, dispatch to the airline.
2	
3	Arguments are names and ids only - never a distance or a price - so the LLM cannot pass a number
4	it made up. Results go back to the LLM as display values; errors are structured records too.
5	
6	There is no booking tool. `Toolbox` keeps only the four bound methods it dispatches to, not the
7	`Airline` object, so nothing in this module can reach `Airline.book` (design P4, rule M04).
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import json
12	import time
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
14	from typing import Any, Callable
15	
16	MAX_ARG_CHARS = 200
17	
18	
19	def _tool(name: str, description: str, properties: dict[str, str], required: list[str]) -> dict:
20	    return {
21	        "type": "function",
22	        "function": {
23	            "name": name,
24	            "description": description,
25	            "parameters": {
26	                "type": "object",
27	                "properties": {k: {"type": "string", "description": v} for k, v in properties.items()},
28	                "required": required,
29	                "additionalProperties": False,
30	            },
31	        },
32	    }
33	
34	
35	TOOL_SCHEMAS = [
36	    _tool("find_city",
37	          "Look up one city: whether Ocean Above flies there, and if not, the nearest cities that "
38	          "have service. Use it when the user asks about a single city.",
39	          {"name": "City name as the user wrote it."}, ["name"]),
40	    _tool("quote_route",
41	          "Find the cheapest route between two cities and create a quote (legs, transfer cities, "
42	          "distance, price). Also reports unknown, ambiguous or unserved cities, with the nearest "
43	          "served cities. Shows a route card to the user.",
44	          {"origin": "Departure city as the user wrote it.",
45	           "destination": "Arrival city as the user wrote it."},
46	          ["origin", "destination"]),
47	    _tool("request_booking",
48	          "Show the user a confirmation card for an existing quote. Call it when the user wants to "
49	          "book a quoted route. It does NOT book: the ticket is issued only when the user clicks "
50	          "Confirm booking on the card.",
51	          {"quote_id": "The quote_id from a quote_route result (starts with q_)."}, ["quote_id"]),
52	    _tool("list_my_tickets",
53	          "List the tickets the user has booked, with the count. All filters are optional.",
54	          {"city": "Only tickets whose origin, destination or a transfer is this city.",
55	           "ticket_id": "Only this ticket (starts with t_).",
56	           "booked_after": "ISO date or datetime (UTC); tickets booked at or after it.",
57	           "booked_before": "ISO date or datetime (UTC); tickets booked before it."},
58	          []),
59	]
60	STATUS_TEXT = {
61	    "find_city": "Looking up the city…",
62	    "quote_route": "Looking up routes…",
63	    "request_booking": "Preparing your confirmation…",
64	    "list_my_tickets": "Looking up your tickets…",
65	}
66	DEFAULT_STATUS = "Working on it…"
67	_SPECS = {t["function"]["name"]: t["function"]["parameters"] for t in TOOL_SCHEMAS}
68	
69	
70	@dataclass(frozen=True)
71	class Outcome:
72	    """One executed (or refused) tool call."""
73	
74	    name: str
75	    args: Any  # parsed arguments, or the raw string when they were not valid JSON
76	    code: str
77	    payload: dict  # the JSON the LLM gets: {"code": ..., display values, names, ids}
78	    cards: tuple[dict, ...] = ()
79	    error: str | None = None  # set for calls that did not run or crashed
80	    latency_ms: int = 0
81	
82	    def for_llm(self) -> str:
83	        return json.dumps(self.payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
84	
85	
86	def slim(value: Any) -> Any:
87	    """Drop the 30-decimal `distance` / `price` strings where a display value sits next to them:
88	    the LLM only ever sees display values."""
89	    if isinstance(value, dict):
90	        return {k: slim(v) for k, v in value.items()
91	                if not (k in ("distance", "price") and f"{k}_display" in value)}
92	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
93	        return [slim(v) for v in value]
94	    return value
95	
96	
97	def _payload(code: str, data: dict) -> dict:
98	    out = {"code": code, **slim(data)}
99	    if isinstance(out.get("legs"), list) and isinstance(out.get("transfers"), list):
100	        # counted here so the LLM never counts (FSR: self-reported counts go wrong)
101	        out["leg_count"] = len(out["legs"])
102	        out["transfer_count"] = len(out["transfers"])
103	    return out
104	
105	
106	def validate(name: str, args: Any) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None]:
107	    """(clean arguments, None) or (None, what is wrong)."""
108	    spec = _SPECS[name]
109	    if not isinstance(args, dict):
110	        return None, "arguments must be a JSON object"
111	    unknown = sorted(set(args) - set(spec["properties"]))
112	    if unknown:
113	        return None, f"unknown argument(s): {', '.join(unknown)}; allowed: {', '.join(spec['properties'])}"
114	    clean: dict[str, str] = {}
115	    for key in spec["properties"]:
116	        value = args.get(key)
117	        if value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip() and key not in spec["required"]):
118	            continue
119	        if not isinstance(value, str):
120	            return None, f"{key} must be a string"
121	        value = value.strip()
122	        if not value:
123	            return None, f"{key} must not be empty"
124	        if len(value) > MAX_ARG_CHARS:
125	            return None, f"{key} is too long"
126	        clean[key] = value
127	    missing = [k for k in spec["required"] if k not in clean]
128	    if missing:
129	        return None, f"missing argument(s): {', '.join(missing)}"
130	    return clean, None
131	
132	
133	class Toolbox:
134	    def __init__(self, airline: Any):
135	        find_city, quote_route = airline.find_city, airline.quote_route
136	        request_booking, list_tickets = airline.request_booking, airline.list_tickets
137	        self._run: dict[str, Callable[[str, str, dict], Any]] = {
138	            "find_city": lambda user, conv, a: find_city(a["name"]),
139	            "quote_route": lambda user, conv, a: quote_route(user, conv, a["origin"], a["destination"]),
140	            "request_booking": lambda user, conv, a: request_booking(user, conv, a["quote_id"]),
141	            "list_my_tickets": lambda user, conv, a: list_tickets(user, **a),
142	        }
143	
144	    def run(self, user_id: str, conversation_id: str, name: str, raw_arguments: str) -> Outcome:
145	        """Validate and execute one tool call. Never raises: every failure is an Outcome the LLM
146	        can read and correct."""
147	        started = time.monotonic()
148	
149	        def refused(code: str, message: str, args: Any, **extra: Any) -> Outcome:
150	            return Outcome(name, args, code, {"code": code, "message": message, **extra},
151	                           error=message, latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
152	
153	        if name not in self._run:
154	            return refused("unknown_tool", f"there is no tool named {name!r}", raw_arguments,
155	                           available=sorted(self._run))
156	        try:
157	            args = json.loads(raw_arguments) if (raw_arguments or "").strip() else {}
158	        except ValueError:
159	            return refused("invalid_arguments", "arguments are not valid JSON", raw_arguments)
160	        clean, problem = validate(name, args)
161	        if clean is None:
162	            return refused("invalid_arguments", problem or "invalid arguments", args)
163	        try:
164	            result = self._run[name](user_id, conversation_id, clean)
165	        except Exception as exc:  # NetworkDataError (locations.db unreadable), NotFound, bugs
166	            failed = refused("tool_failed", "the tool could not run; flight data may be unavailable", clean)
167	            return replace(failed, error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"[:500])
168	        return Outcome(name, clean, result.code, _payload(result.code, result.data),
169	                       tuple(result.cards), latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
170
